text:
priya: Heads-up — did an initial bring-up of qwen-mini-13b-v2 int4 on dedicated pool. Throughput/latency looks fine but eval shows a weird accuracy regression on longer contexts (MMLU/BBH). baseline fp16 -> int4 drop ~3.7% on MMLU, mostly after ~1k tokens. sharing artifacts and quick notes.

drew: Link?

priya: https://artifacts.internal/reports/8401234567 — contains eval CSV, per-head attn dumps, and quant calibration logs.

sasha: Thanks. Any obvious tokenization mismatch (BPE offsets) or conversion script logs?

priya: Tokenizer matches (used our qwen-convert v0.9). Conversion log shows no decoder errors, but the attn head dumps reveal a repeating phase offset in ~6/32 heads. Looks like a headwise phase shear.

jason: Could this be a rotary/scale mismatch? qwen variants sometimes ship with nonstandard rotary_scale params.

priya: I thought so. I compared the rotary coeffs vs gemma baseline and qwen's table has a small fractional phase drift that accumulates with position index. Patch snippet I used to dump:

```
# dump head phases (toy)
for h in range(num_heads):
    phases = model.attn.rotary[h][:16]  # first 16 freqs
    print(h, [round(float(x),6) for x in phases[:6]])
```

priya: grep output:

```
0 [0.000785, 0.001571, 0.002356, 0.003142, 0.003927, 0.004713]
1 [0.000790, 0.001580, 0.002369, 0.003158, 0.003947, 0.004736]  # +5e-06 drift
5 [0.000805, 0.001610, 0.002415, 0.003221, 0.004027, 0.004833]  # accumulates
```

drew: Small per-head bias like that can break int4 K/V cache alignment after quantization noise. Did you see any KV-cache token-id off-by-one traces?

priya: Yes — in longctx replay traces some cached keys produced logits identical to previous token for a few steps, then corrected. Looks like transient aliasing.

sasha: Reminds me of the \"phase-shear\" issue we saw on orpheus-lite — solution back then was to: 1) force rotary_scale to None on load, 2) apply per-head linear correction (subtract head_bias * pos_idx), 3) re-run quant calibration with extended warmup (5k steps).

priya: I'll try that. Two tests planned: (A) fix rotary/table only + int4 recalib, (B) fallback to int8 quant for heads that show >threshold drift. Which should I prioritize?

drew: Try A first — cheaper. If still bad, B. I'll queue a 4h run on dpool-7 now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary job queued on dpool-7, job_id=dp-8401, ETA ~4h.

jason: Also add a quick eval: prompt windows 512/1024/2048 and check top-1 token shifts and coherence (n-gram overlap). If we see consistent prefix collapse, that's a red flag for kv aliasing.

priya: Good call. I'll include top-1 token delta histograms in the artifact bundle.

sasha: If A works, we should add a conversion safety-check that normalizes rotary tables to a canonical float dtype before quant. Might avoid repeats in future.

priya: Agreed — filing a tiny RFC after the run. For now reassigning @drew to run compute and I'll own eval/analysis.

drew: On it — starting job now. Will ping on completion.

priya: :thumbsup: thanks all, will follow-up with results and the new artifact link.

(7m later) drew: quick update — job started, seeing expected perf. calibration logs show bit patterns consistent with per-head variance; saving intermediate dumps to artifacts.

(3h later) priya: First pass results: A (rotary normalize + recalib int4) cuts drop from 3.7% -> 0.9% on MMLU, longctx prefix collapse gone in most cases. Posting full CSV: https://artifacts.internal/reports/8401234567-passA.csv

sasha: Nice! Still want to run B on a small sample to compare cost/quality.

priya: Will queue B tomorrow. For now flagging model as \"int4-viable with rotary-normalize\" in onboarding notes. I'll add conversion check and a short how-to in model-meta.

jason: Great triage. Can we add a regression eval to run on every conversion that checks these longctx histograms?

priya: Yep — adding to CI checklist.

ops-bot: incident-bot: no incidents triggered.

sasha: thx team.
